result:
The proposed formulas grow quadratically in n, but the minimum is only linear in n.

The condition says every pair of cities has at least two common neighbours. A construction with a hub shows this:

- Join one hub vertex v to all other cities, which uses n−1 roads.
- On the remaining n−1 cities, use a windmill-type graph in which every pair has a common neighbour and every vertex has degree at least 2. This costs about 3(n−2)/2 roads.
- Every pair then has the hub as one common neighbour and a second one inside the windmill part. The pair (v, x) gets its two common neighbours from the two neighbours of x in the windmill part.

This gives roughly (5n−8)/2 roads, which is about 2.5n. This is far smaller than the proposed n(n−2)/2, which is about n²/2. For example, at n = 20 the construction needs about 46 roads, not 180. So the proposed S(n) is wrong for n ≥ 10, and the sum 1130 is wrong.

VERDICT: REJECT
